In the Name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surat ad-Dukhan

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night﴾.

Here Allah, exalted is He, left this blessed night unspecified, but He made clear that it is the Night of Decree (laylat al-qadr) in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Decree﴾ [al-Qadr: 1]. And He made clear that it is the "blessed" one mentioned here in His saying: ﴿The Night of Decree is better than a thousand months﴾ [al-Qadr: 3], to the end of the surah.

So His saying ﴿in a blessed night﴾ means: abounding in blessings and goods.

There is no doubt that a night which is better than a thousand months, with all the attributes described for it in Surat al-Qadr, is abounding in blessings and goods to an extreme degree.

Allah has also made clear that this blessed night is the Night of Decree, in which the Qur'an was sent down in the month of Ramadan, in His saying: ﴿The month of Ramadan in which the Qur'an was sent down﴾ [al-Baqarah: 185].

Therefore the claim that it is the night of the middle of Sha'ban, as related from 'Ikrimah and others, is without doubt a false claim, because it contradicts the clear text of the Qur'an.

And there is no doubt that everything that opposes the truth is false.

As for the hadiths which some of them cite to the effect that it is in Sha'ban, those which contradict the clear text of the Qur'an have no basis, and the chain of none of them is sound, as Ibn al-'Arabi and not a few of the verifying scholars (muhaqqiqun) affirmed with certainty.

So it is most astonishing that a Muslim should contradict the clear text of the Qur'an without a basis in the Book or in a sound Sunnah.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 44, verse 4:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿In it every decree of wisdom is made distinct, a command from Us﴾.

The meaning of His saying "yufraqu" (is made distinct) is: it is separated out and made clear, and written down, on the blessed night which is the Night of Decree (Laylat al-Qadr), every matter of wisdom (amrin hakim), i.e., one possessing far-reaching wisdom, because everything that Allah does encompasses kinds of marvellous wisdom.

Some of them said: "hakim" means "muhkam" (firm, perfected), with no alteration or change in it.

(p-173) Both meanings are true, because what has preceded in Allah's knowledge does not change or alter, and because all of His acts are in the utmost wisdom.

In terminology, wisdom (hikmah) is placing matters in their proper places and bringing them about in their right positions.

The clarification of the meaning of the verse is that Allah, blessed and exalted, in every Night of Decree of the year, makes clear to the angels and writes for them, in detail and with explanation, everything that will occur in that year until the Night of Decree of the new year.

Thus there are made clear in it the terms of life, the provisions, poverty and wealth, fertility and barrenness, health and sickness, wars and earthquakes, and everything that will occur in that year, whatever it may be.

Al-Zamakhshari said in al-Kashshaf: The meaning of "yufraqu" is: it is separated out and written down, every matter of wisdom concerning the provisions and terms of the servants and all their affairs in it until the next one that comes. Until he said: So the copy of the provisions is handed to Mika'il, the copy of wars to Jibril, and likewise earthquakes, thunderbolts and landslides, and the copy of deeds to Isma'il, lord of the lowest heaven, who is a great angel, and the copy of calamities to the Angel of Death. End of quotation, the relevant point, in his own words.

Our aim is to explain the meaning of the verse, not to commit to the soundness of handing those copies to the angels named, since we do not know a basis for it.

This meaning indicated by this noble verse also indicates that the blessed night is the Night of Decree; so it is another Qur'anic clarification.

The clarification of that is that the meaning of His saying: ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Decree﴾ is: during the night of determination for all the affairs of the year, of provision and death, life and birth, sickness and health, fertility and barrenness, and other than that of all the affairs of the year.

Some of them said: Even a man marries, conducts his affairs, and has children born to him, while his name has already been listed among the dead for that year.

According to this correct interpretation of the Night of Decree, the determination mentioned is precisely what is meant by His saying: ﴿In it every decree of wisdom is made distinct﴾.

(p-174) We have already mentioned in the surah "al-Anbiya'", in discussing His saying: ﴿So he thought that We would not decree upon him﴾ [al-Anbiya': 87], that "qadara" with a fatha on the dal, lightened, yaqdiru, and "yaqduru" and "yaqdiru" with kasra and damma, like yadribu and yansuru, with the verbal noun qadran, meaning qaddara taqdiran (decreed), and that Tha'lab recited for this the saying of the poet:

"Those evenings of the pasture will never return to us, however delightful the fresh peace is.
Nor will that time that has passed return. Blessed are You; whatever You decree occurs, and to You is thanks."

We clarified there that this is the meaning of the Night of Decree, because Allah decrees therein the events of the year.

We also clarified that this is the meaning of His saying: ﴿In it every decree of wisdom is made distinct﴾, and we explained there that "al-qadar" with a fatha on the dal and "al-qadr" with its sukun are what Allah decrees of His judgement. From this is the saying of Hudhba ibn al-Khashram:

"Alas, O my people, for calamities and decree, and for a matter that a man encounters from where he does not know."

Know that the saying of one who said: The night was named "Laylat al-Qadr" only because of its greatness and its nobility over other nights, from their saying: "So-and-so has qadr", meaning he has nobility and an elevated standing, does not contradict the first saying, since it is characterized by both matters together, and the validity of describing it by each of them, as we have explained similar things many times.

The scholars differed over the grammatical analysis (i'rab) of His saying: ﴿a command from Us﴾. Some of them said: It is a indefinite verbal noun (masdar munakkar) in the position of a circumstantial qualifier (hal), meaning: We sent it down while We were commanding by it.

Al-Akhfash is among those who said this.

Some of them said: It is what stands in for the absolute object (mutlaq) from His saying "anzalnahu" (We sent it down), and "amran" is taken to mean "inzalan" (sending down).

Al-Mubarrad is among those who said this.

Some of them said it is what stands in for the absolute object from "yufraqu", so "amran" is taken to mean "farqan" (distinction), or "farqun" is taken to mean "amran". 

Al-Farra' and al-Zajjaj are among those who said this.

Some of them said it is a circumstantial qualifier (hal) from "amran", meaning: "yufraqu fiha bayna kulli amrin hakim" (it is made distinct therein between every matter of wisdom) while it is "amran min 'indina" (a command from Us). This view is good and evident, and bringing a circumstantial qualifier from an indefinite noun that is placed after it is permissible, because the indefinite noun "amrun" is qualified by "hakim", as is not hidden.

Some of them said "amran" is an object (maf'ul bihi) of "mundhirin" (warners) from the verse [al-Dukhan: 3]. Others said other than that.

Al-Zamakhshari chose that it is in the accusative by way of specification (ikhtisas), saying: He made every matter stately and grand, by describing it as "hakim", then increased its eloquence and gave it majesty, by saying: "I mean by this matter a matter originating from Us, existing from Our presence, as Our knowledge and governance require." This view is also possible, and knowledge is with Allah, exalted.

The words of Allah Most High: ﴿Indeed, We were ever sending [warners]﴾ ﴿as a mercy from your Lord﴾.

We have already presented the clarifying verses concerning this in Surah "al-Kahf," in the discussion of His words Most High: ﴿So they found a servant from among Our servants, whom We had given mercy from Us﴾ [al-Kahf: 65]. And in Surah "Fatir," in the discussion of His words Most High: ﴿Whatever mercy Allah grants to the people, none can withhold it﴾ [Fatir: 2].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 44, verse 14:

Allah's words: ﴿Then they turned away from him and said, "A taught one, a madman."﴾

This that they alleged against the Prophet ﷺ, that he is "taught" (mu'allam), is a fabrication. They mean that a human being taught him this Qur'an, and that the Prophet ﷺ is a madman. We have already explained the verses that clarify its refutation.

As for their claim that he is "taught," we have already presented the verses that indicate this claim in Surat an-Nahl, in the discussion of His words: ﴿And We certainly know that they say, "It is only a human being who teaches him."﴾ [an-Nahl: 103]. And in Surat al-Furqan, in the discussion of His words: ﴿And those who disbelieve say, "This is nothing but a lie he has fabricated, and other people have helped him with it,"﴾ up to His words ﴿and it is dictated to him morning and evening﴾ [al-Furqan: 4-5].

We have also explained the verses that clarify their lying and obstinacy in Surat an-Nahl, in the discussion of His words: ﴿The tongue of the one they refer to is foreign, while this is a clear Arabic tongue﴾ [an-Nahl: 103].

And in al-Furqan, in the discussion of His words: ﴿So they have committed injustice and falsehood, and said, "Myths of the former peoples, which he has had written down"﴾ up to the verse [al-Furqan: 4-5].

As for their claim that he is a madman, we have already presented the verses that clarify it and refute it in Surat ﴿Qad aflaha al-mu'minun﴾ (The Believers), in the discussion of His words: ﴿Or do they say, "There is madness in him"? Rather, he has brought them the truth﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 70].

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And there came to them a noble messenger﴾ ﴿saying: "Deliver to me the servants of Allah"﴾.

The noble messenger is Musa (Moses), and the verses showing that Musa is the one who was sent to Pharaoh and his people are numerous and well known.

His saying: ﴿Deliver to me﴾ means: hand over to me the servants of Allah, meaning the Children of Israel, and send them with me.

So his saying: ﴿servants of Allah﴾ is the direct object (maf'ul bihi) of his saying: أدّوا (adda', "deliver").

What this noble verse includes, that Musa asked Pharaoh to hand over the Children of Israel to him and send them with him, is made clear in other verses, which state explicitly that the servants of Allah are the Children of Israel. Such as His saying, Exalted is He, in Surah Ta-Ha: ﴿So go to him and say: "We are two messengers of your Lord, so send with us the Children of Israel and do not torment them"﴾ [Ta-Ha: 47]. And His saying, Exalted is He, in Surah ash-Shu'ara': ﴿So go to Pharaoh and say: "We are messengers of the Lord of the worlds"﴾ ﴿"that you send with us the Children of Israel"﴾, and the verse [ash-Shu'ara': 16-17].

The verified view is that أنْ (an) in his saying ﴿أن أدّوا﴾ is the explanatory (mufassirah, an "an" that explains what precedes it), because the coming of the messenger contains the meaning of saying, and not the lightened form (mukhaffafah min al-thaqilah, "an" lightened from "anna"). Also, his saying ﴿servants of Allah﴾ is a direct object, as we have mentioned, and as the verse of Ta-Ha and the verse of ash-Shu'ara' have made clear, and not a vocative construct (munada mudaf, a vocative followed by a genitive noun).

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And indeed I have sought refuge in my Lord and your Lord﴾.

We have already presented the discussion of this in Surah "al-Mu'min" (Ghafir), in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And Moses said, "Indeed I have sought refuge in my Lord and your Lord from every arrogant one who does not believe in the Day of Reckoning."﴾ [Ghafir: 27].

Allah's saying: ﴿Thus did We cause another people to inherit them﴾.

He does not specify here who these people are whom He made to inherit what is mentioned here; however, He clarified in Surah "al-Shu'ara'" that they are the Children of Israel, in His saying: ﴿Thus did We cause the Children of Israel to inherit them﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 59], as was previously mentioned in the chapter heading, and in "al-A'raf" (also).

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 44, verse 30:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We certainly delivered the Children of Israel from the humiliating torment﴾ ﴿from Pharaoh. Indeed, he was haughty and among the transgressors.﴾

What He, glorified and exalted is He, mentioned in this noble verse, that He delivered the Children of Israel from the humiliating torment with which Pharaoh and his people used to torment them, has been clarified in other verses, in which the kinds of the aforementioned torment are explicitly stated,

such as His saying, exalted is He, in Surat al-Baqarah: ﴿And [recall] when We delivered you from the people of Pharaoh, who put you to the worst torment, slaughtering your sons and keeping your women alive. And in that was a great trial from your Lord﴾ up to His saying: ﴿while you were watching﴾ [al-Baqarah: 49-50].

And His saying in al-A'raf: ﴿And [recall] when We delivered you from the people of Pharaoh, who put you to the worst torment, killing your sons﴾, the verse [al-A'raf: 141].

And His saying, exalted is He, in al-Mu'min: ﴿So when he brought them the truth from Us, they said, "Kill the sons of those who believe with him"﴾, the verse [Ghafir: 25].

And His saying, exalted is He, concerning Moses (regarding the speech of Moses to his people): ﴿And [recall] when Moses said to his people, "Remember the favor of Allah upon you when He delivered you from the people of Pharaoh, who put you to the worst torment and slaughtered your sons"﴾, the verse [Ibrahim: 16].

And His saying in al-Shu'ara': ﴿And this is a favor of which you remind me, that you have enslaved the Children of Israel﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 22]. So his enslaving them is among the kinds of torment he inflicted upon them, along with other verses.

And what He, glorified and exalted is He, mentioned in this noble verse, that Pharaoh was haughty and among the transgressors, He also clarified in other places, such as His saying, exalted is He, in Yunus: ﴿Indeed, Pharaoh was haughty in the land, and indeed he was among the transgressors﴾ [Yunus: 83]. And His saying, exalted is He, at the beginning of al-Qasas: ﴿Indeed, Pharaoh exalted himself in the land and made its people factions, oppressing a group of them, slaughtering their sons and keeping their women alive. Indeed, he was among the corrupters﴾ [al-Qasas: 4]. Along with other verses.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Then pour over his head some of the torment of the boiling water﴾.

We have already presented the clarifying verses in Surah al-Hajj, in discussing His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Boiling water will be poured over their heads﴾ [al-Hajj: 19].

(p-178) We have omitted many cross-references in which we explained some verses of this Surah, al-Dukhan, out of concern for prolixity through an abundance of cross-referencing.

The author said in *Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab* (Removing the Appearance of Contradiction from the Verses of the Book):

(p-388) In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah al-Dukhan

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Then pour over his head some of the torment of the boiling water﴾ ﴿Taste it; indeed you were the mighty, the noble!﴾.

This noble verse may give the impression, from its apparent meaning, that the people of the Fire possess might and nobility, even though the Quranic verses explicitly state otherwise, such as His saying: ﴿They will enter Hell humiliated﴾ [Ghafir: 60], meaning contemptible and abased; and His saying: ﴿And for them is a humiliating punishment﴾ [Al 'Imran: 178]; and His saying here: ﴿Seize him and drag him into the midst of Hell﴾ [al-Dukhan: 47].

The answer is that it was revealed concerning Abu Jahl when he said: "Does Muhammad (ﷺ) threaten me, when between its two mountains there is no one mightier or more noble than me?" So when God punished him for his disbelief, He said to him: ﴿Taste it; indeed you were the mighty, the noble!﴾, meaning in your false claim. Rather, you are the humiliated, the base, the contemptible. This rebuke is thus a kind of punishment.

Allah's statement: ﴿So We have made it easy only in your tongue, that they may remember﴾.

We have already presented the clarifying verses in Surah "Maryam" in the discussion of His statement, ﴿So We have made it easy only in your tongue, that you may give glad tidings thereby to the righteous﴾ [Maryam: 97], the verse.
